questions.prompt: A bracket has FoS = 11 under its static payload. What does this prove about the design?
options: Nothing about other load cases: each declared case needs its own check, and the worst governs
The design is verified for all load cases, because 11 is far above one in this case
It can be given a factor of safety of 11 in every other load case too, by the same margin
It proves that the stiffness is adequate, since the stress and the stiffness agree here
questions.explanation: Verification is relative to the declared load envelope; dynamic and actuator-peak cases may govern.

questions.prompt: Cantilever, F = 29.43 N, L = 0.10 m, b = 0.020 m, h = 0.006 m. Root bending stress in MPa (three decimals)?
Same bracket, aluminium sigma_y = 276 MPa under F = 294.3 N. Factor of safety (three decimals)?
sigma = 100 MPa and tau = 50 MPa at a point. Von Mises stress in MPa (two decimals)?
The thickness h of a rectangular cantilever is halved with everything else equal. What happens to the bending stress and tip deflection?
Which check is an INDEPENDENT verification of a hand-calculated bracket stress?
options: A strain-gauge test or a separate FEA with a different formulation
Re-running the same spreadsheet with the same inputs and formulas
Asking the author to review their own numbers once more by hand
Copying the formula into a second cell and comparing the two results
questions.explanation: Independence means a different method or person, not a repeat of the same calculation.

questions.prompt: List four load cases you would declare for a robot wrist bracket and for each the source of the load and the check you would perform.
rubric: Names distinct cases such as static payload, operating acceleration, emergency stop at actuator peak torque, collision/impact, fatigue cycles.
Gives each case's source (gravity, motion profile, motor peak torque from the gearbox, impact energy).
Pairs each with an allowable (FoS, deflection) and an independent check.
